static_traits.name: Li Wendi
static_traits.social_status: Has a few close friends but has not yet confided worries about the divorce and future relationships to them; avoids socializing and developing new relationships for fear of being hurt again
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before the divorce; no previous psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Positive attitude, highly cooperative; able to express clearly and identify inner dialogue and automatic thoughts; clear thinking, good logic; slightly tense but hopeful

basic_info.main_problem: Because of a past divorce, I believe I will never marry and be happy again, which makes me feel despair and hopelessness.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these negative thoughts about relationships are affecting my overall well-being and causing distress; I really want to change the way I think and feel.
growth_experiences: Experienced a divorce two years ago; felt extreme stress, heartbreak, and being lost ('feeling I did not know who I was') after the divorce. These feelings have persisted since, repeatedly reactivated when seeing happy couples, with the belief 'I will never marry and be happy again'. The event has long affected life: avoiding socializing and developing new relationships, fearing heartbreak again, sleep and eating patterns affected, decline in work performance, and difficulty opening up to close friends about the divorce and worries about future relationships.

core_beliefs: Divorced people do not deserve happiness

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others are all happy in relationships and I am divorced, it means I will never have the chance for the same happiness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social and relationship settings, looking away or displacing attention, throwing oneself into work and hobbies to distract from emotions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: That happiness has nothing to do with me; I will never marry or be happy again

special_situations.event: Considering whether to start a new intimate relationship
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try intimacy again, I will surely be heartbroken and rejected again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Withdrawing in advance and avoiding building new relationships to avoid potential hurt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will get hurt again; better not to start, it is safer

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being divorced equals failure; failures do not deserve to be loved
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Labeling oneself, judging the self by extreme standards to 'remind' oneself not to try again

special_situations.event: Successfully saving a patient at work and gaining recognition
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Workplace worth has nothing to do with being loved; this positive evidence cannot change the reality of being destined for loneliness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating and devaluing positive evidence, quickly shifting attention back to negative predictions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These do not count; my relationships still will not improve

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be loved and accepted, longing to rebuild a safe and stable intimate relationship
core_conflict.fear: Fear of heartbreak and rejection again; worried that exposing vulnerability will bring hurt and shame
defense_goal: Reduces the risk of getting hurt by keeping distance and avoiding intimacy
Presses painful emotions down by investing in work and hobbies, maintaining a superficial sense of control and stability

object_relations.object_representation: Potential partners/others are people who may hurt and reject oneself

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling goes deep into the divorce experience and vulnerable feelings about future relationships
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worries that exposing vulnerability will lead to being judged or hurt again, so I need to press the pain down
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, empathize first then clarify; allow pauses and emotional expression, use open questions to invite describing current bodily feelings and emotions, do not rush for details, give safe boundaries and choices.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to try small-scale socializing outside the session or share feelings with a trusted person
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing attempts as high-risk, worrying about being rejected or losing self-control, thus postponing or canceling with excuses like 'busy / having no time'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use a supportive, collaborative tone with a motivational-interviewing style, affirming the caution and self-protection; work with the client to make goals tiny, emphasizing optionality and reversibility to lower the sense of threat.

manifestations: The belief 'I am destined for loneliness' recurring after the divorce
Avoiding socializing and developing new relationships, finding it hard to open up to close friends about the divorce and worries about the future
Feeling 'I did not know who I was' after the divorce; role and identity shaken
Positive moments (such as treating patients) are hard to internalize as a lasting sense of self-worth
outcomes: Inner emptiness and sense of loss
Lowered hope for the future; work affected by emotional distress

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I will just endure it', 'I should not trouble others', and so on
manifestations: Wanting closeness and support yet choosing to bear it alone, not confiding post-divorce feelings to close friends
Avoiding new relationships, channeling energy into self-restraint and repression

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Labeling oneself 'unlovable / a failure', with excessive self-blame and self-restriction
Excessively worrying about being rejected before socializing, thus being overcautious or even withdrawing

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact, corresponding to 'acceptance'. Language manifestations include: 'Speaking of which... haha, just kidding', 'In theory...', and so on
manifestations: Distracting through work and hobbies to avoid directly touching sadness, loneliness, and the fear of being rejected
After positive moments appear, quickly shifts attention away, finding it hard to stay with and absorb positive feelings

exception_events.target_problem: When facing intimacy and self-worth issues, the client usually falls into the thought 'I am not loved / destined for loneliness', developing despair and avoidance of socializing.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At the moment of successfully saving a patient in the ER, the client did not fall into the old self-evaluation of 'I am worthless', but instead experienced 'I am very capable, needed and recognized'; the positive feeling was not lasting but clearly felt.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the situation had clear goals and visible results (successful rescue) bringing immediate positive feedback, activating competence and worth, thus weakening the negative self-narrative about 'being destined for loneliness / being unlovable' in the moment.

positive_force: Experiences competence and recognition in professional settings, which can activate a sense of value
Clear motivation for help and a positive attitude, willing to change thoughts and behaviors
Able to identify and verbalize automatic thoughts, with some self-awareness
Maintains daily activities and hobbies, with a certain degree of life structure and capacity for action
Has a few close friends as potential support resources
negative_force: Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, predicting the future, and black-and-white thinking reinforce hopelessness
Avoidance of intimate relationships maintains the self-confirming cycle of loneliness and negative beliefs
Fear of heartbreak again leads to unwillingness to try and expose vulnerability
Sleep and diet affected, work impaired, further weakening self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding socializing and avoiding developing new relationships
antecedent: Thinking of starting a new relationship or being invited to socialize
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong fear of heartbreak and rejection again after the divorce trauma, maintained by cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing and predicting the future
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential emotional hurt and uncertainty, thus relieving anxiety in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent loneliness and isolation, negative beliefs self-confirmed, decreased quality of life and decreased sense of happiness

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated negative thinking about marriage and happiness (catastrophizing and the 'never happy again' self-suggestion)
target_behavior.core_reason: Shaken self-identity from the divorce and activated traumatic memories, with black-and-white and predicting-the-future cognitive biases
target_behavior.function: Gaining a 'preemptive defense' sense of control and false early warning of risks, reducing anxiety from uncertainty in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Worsening despair and hopelessness, impaired sleep and diet, decline in work performance, social avoidance further reinforced
